There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

</system-reminder>

7107:- **2026-10-15 — Cyrus live build progress + progress-based timeouts (branch `feature/cyrus-live-progress`, not merged, not deployed, no migration; build-service image bump REQUIRED: services/modbuilder changed).** The 600 s per-call / 1200 s per-build wall clocks are replaced by inactivity supervision (`MB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` 300, ceilings `MB_CALL_CEILING_S` 14400 / `MB_BUILD_CEILING_S` 21600; the old env names still work as explicit overrides) and a call killed after it wrote files gets one continuation instead of failing; builds expose an honest activity feed (`progress`: phase, file, sanitized hint, counters, coalesced heartbeats) that the studio trace and project page render with relative times and a "still working, the model is thinking" state after 60 s of quiet. Portal: `lib/cyrus/builder/progress-view.ts`, `components/cyrus/prompt/BuildActivity.tsx`; STALE_MS now counts from last sync; follow stream 6.5 h. Details in docs/cyrus/07-operations.md.
7108:- **2026-10-14 — Cyrus structure round: workspace map for change builds, structural perf rules + verified rewrite, Paper member index + did-you-mean, Q1 eval lane labels (branch `feature/cyrus-structure`, not merged, not deployed, build-service flags `MB_WORKSPACE_MAP` / `MB_AST_PERF` / `MB_MEMBER_INDEX` all off, needs image redeploy, no migration).** New dependency-free Java structure reader (`services/modbuilder/javaast.js`); `astperf.js` detects spawn/drop/summon in loops of every shape, forEach/stream lambdas and fast timers and wraps them in `NxPerf.spawnAllowed` (real javac: 84 compiles, 0 regressions); `memberindex.js` + `tools/gen-member-index.js` (javap index at image build) fix unambiguous hallucinated names and shrink repair hints; `workspacemap.js` puts a capped outline of the project in the first turn of change builds. `cov-tablist`, `cov-warps`, `cov-playtime-rewards`, `cov-bossbar-titles` are plain-lane eval prompts. Details: docs/cyrus/02-engine.md#structure-round-workspace-map-structural-perf-rules-member-index.
7109:- **2026-10-14 — Cyrus behaviour oracle (oracle-1, branch `feature/cyrus-behaviour-oracle`, NOT merged, NOT deployed, `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_ORACLE` OFF, no migration, no image bump).** Test Flight now also asks "does the mod do what it says": `lib/cyrus/testflight/oracle` derives declarative expectations per build from plugin.yml, config.yml and the designer / data pack / rig specs (no model call; optional model extras off), flies them in the SAME flight (optional RCON checks `nxo-*` + scripted-player scenarios `T-901..`, budget 45 s + 15 s join) and judges each pass / fail / not_run / not_testable with evidence; stored as `ModBuild.cyrus.testFlight.functional` (never changes the boot verdict or the install block; oracle errors = not_run). New playtest steps (look_at, attack_entity, click_window, close_window, use_item.holdMs, expect_window/particle/sound/bossbar/sidebar, action bar packet). Portal project page card "What we verified"; eval stage `behaviour` + `behaves` (`eval-run --oracle`), journal stats. Real flights: `scripts/cyrus/oracle-flight.ts`. See docs/cyrus/16-behaviour-oracle.md.
7111:- **2026-10-14 — Email rollout: every email on shell v2, the 7 remaining mockup designs, accurate socials/data, image audit (branch `feature/nx-marketing-emails`, not merged, not deployed, no migration).** `wrapEmail()` now renders shell v2 for EVERY email (code-built catalog, DB-template bodies, worker/admin sends): a body that leads with the legacy eyebrow / headline / short lead paragraph is lifted into the hero band (per-game key art when the template names a game family, otherwise the default beams plus a 64px badge image from `public/email/badges/`), the remaining v1 components (`emailPanel`, `emailKeyValue`, `emailList`, `emailBanner`, `emailButton` full width, ...) are restyled to the mockup. `lib/email-build.ts` holds the shared `build()` (template to badge map, optional `gameFamily` + compact "this server" row with the game tile). Mockup designs in `lib/email-designs.ts`: welcome, invoice (items, subtotal/total, Pay Invoice, Auto Pay explainer when unpaid or known off), renewal ("Renews in N days" card, server row, no-downtime card, game banner), Cyrus announcement (new `emails.cyrusAnnouncement`), datacenter expansion (new `emails.datacenterExpansion`), tips and guides (new `emails.tipsGuides`), partner program (`emails.creatorPartnerInvite`). New catalog entries are in `lib/email-samples.ts`, `app/admin/mail/templates/page.tsx` (preview rail, plus a generic "More" group so no sample is missing) and can be test-sent to the signed-in admin only via `sendTemplateTestToSelf` ("Send test to me" in the preview). NEVER-INVENT RULE: numbers come from `lib/email-stats.ts` (pure) fed by `lib/email-data.ts` (enabled `Node` regions: locations/continents; pooled `ServerUptimeDaily` over 30 days, shown only with >= 14 measured days and >= 1000 samples; newest published `BlogPost` rows for guides). Absent data omits the tile or line. Per-game images: renewal, dunning (card declined/retry/final, PayPal, 3-D Secure, card re-add), suspended, terminated, backup/restore, provision failed/ready, abuse, auto-reboot, review request accept `gameFamily`; live senders pass it via `emailGameFamilyFor(serverId)`. SOCIALS: the footer row is a marker (`<!--nx-socials-->`) that `sendMail` fills from `getSocialLinks()` (Admin Settings `social_*`, the same helper the marketing footer `NxmFooter` uses); unset means no icons, preview fixtures use only the Discord invite the site already links. TRACKING UNCHANGED (pixel, click rewrite with UTM, unsubscribe link and List-Unsubscribe one-click headers, secret-link exemption); `mailTestHooks.capture` (mailer.ts) lets tests run every template through the real `sendMail` path without delivery. Images (`scripts/email-assets-designs.py`, `scripts/email-assets-optimize.py`): badges, welcome/gift/globe art (globe drawn from `public/countries-110m.json`), Cyrus banner + logo, email-sized posters (replace the webp service chips and the large poster art in the promo email), guide thumbnails; all PNG/JPG, tiles under 15 KB, JPG under 120 KB, public/email about 2.3 MB. Tests: `test/email-rollout.test.ts` (every sample + non-catalog sender through sendMail capture, image files exist, socials, stats, asset budget, Cyrus mail) and the extended `test/fixtures/email-tracking-inventory.json` (now also carries an `unsubscribe` flag per template). The Cyrus notification mail (`lib/cyrus/notify/templates.ts`) got the new structure (header row, hero eyebrow/headline, full-width gradient button) in its own palette. Previews: `NODE_PATH=... tsx scripts/email-preview.ts DIR --png` then `python3 scripts/email-contact-sheets.py DIR`.
7112:- **2026-10-14 — Email template overhaul (branch `feature/nx-marketing-emails`, not merged, not deployed, no migration, no setting).** Every automated email now renders on ONE shared dark "Nexion" shell in `lib/email-render.ts` (`wrapEmail`): logo header with product links, navy card with a violet-to-cyan accent edge, icon tiles, violet gradient buttons, footer (links, address, copyright). Table-based, inline CSS, 600px fluid, `color-scheme: dark light`. Component API unchanged (`emailButton`, `emailPanel`, `emailKeyValue`, `emailList`, ...) plus `emailIconTile`, `emailFeatureRows`; `BRAND` tokens re-valued (new `link`). Bare anchors/bold and legacy light-theme hex in DB-stored bodies are remapped to readable colours. Rebuilt on the shell: flash sale, TRIAL798 promo, GPU restock, VM-move notice, growth scoreboard; new `emails.budgetAlert` (replaces the inline fallback in `lib/spend-caps.ts`, which also had a relative, untrackable link). The Cyrus notification mail (`lib/cyrus/notify/templates.ts`) got the same structure, self-contained (host seam) and keeps its Cyrus palette. The plain-text alternative is now `htmlToText()` (no CSS leakage, links as `label (url)`). Left alone on purpose: cold/outreach mail (`lib/outreach/*`, `lib/coldemail/*`, creator outreach) which is deliberately plain with its own compliance footer, and the admin report digest. TRACKING UNCHANGED: open pixel, `/api/track/email/<id>/click/<n>` rewrite, secret-link exemption, `List-Unsubscribe` + one-click post all still live in `lib/mailer.ts` and every template's own unsubscribe link is kept. Guard: `test/email-templates-overhaul.test.ts` renders every template (`lib/email-samples.ts`, fails if a catalog key lacks a sample) and asserts the pre-overhaul link inventory (`test/fixtures/email-tracking-inventory.json`, captured from main) is preserved, pixel/click rewrite works and secret links stay direct. Preview all: `scripts/email-preview.ts`; inventory dump: `scripts/email-inventory.ts`.

## Core studio UX round (2026-10-15, branch `feature/cyrus-studio-ux`, NOT merged / deployed; one additive table, SQL not applied)
Owner list items 1-6 for the core studio (`/dashboard/cyrus` on Nxeon, `/studio` on cyrus.my). Audit and screenshots: `agent-notes/cyrus-research/CO-studio-ux-audit-2026-10-15.md`.
- **Cut-off pages (3).** Root cause: `.cyrus-root` (studio.css) is a clipped, fixed-height box (`overflow: hidden`, `contain: layout paint`, `container-type: size`) because the studio canvas fills it; the customer app (`.cx-app`, app.css) only had `min-height: 100%`, so it grew past the box and everything below the fold was cut off on both hosts (Nxeon: also the rail's account row). Fix in `app/dashboard/cyrus/app/app.css`: `.cx-app` is its own scroll container (`height: 100%; overflow-y: auto`), the rail is `100cqh` tall, the aura is `position: fixed`, the phone tab bar stays sticky at the bottom. Pure CSS, default on.
- **Menu and way back (5).** `components/cyrus/chrome/StudioNav.tsx` (hamburger in the studio top bar): view switch, Home / New mod / Projects / My assets / Servers / Wallet / Account / Help (host-aware paths; the app links only when `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP=1`, passed down as `appOn`), and the way back: "Back to the Nxeon portal" (last portal page, never the studio) inside Nxeon, "Back to Cyrus home" + "Back to Nxeon" on cyrus.my. Logic is pure (`studioNavLinks`).
- **Simple view (4).** Switch in that menu. `components/cyrus/chrome/SimpleView.tsx` replaces only the constellation canvas with a plain grouped list of the SAME mods; the prompt dock, preview panel, palette, token chip and every build/install action stay. Saved per user (below). Not the customer app's "Simple" (that is a different, separate page set); both exist.
- **Draggable mod branches + Load more (1).** Individual mod pills now drag on their own (before, grabbing one dragged the whole category list); offsets from the pill's list slot are stored in the same `layout` map as game/category branches (key = node id). "+N more" now loads the next page (6 mods) onto the branch and the count per category is kept (`more`). Palette "Reset branch positions" clears the lot.
- **Saved to the profile (1, 4).** `CyrusStudioPref` (userId PK, `prefs` JSON `{ layout, simple, more }`, additive, no FK; SQL `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-15-cyrus-studio-prefs.sql`, NOT applied). Route `app/api/cyrus/studio-prefs` (GET, POST patch; same gate as the studio; same-origin writes; sizes capped; `parseStudioPrefs` in `lib/cyrus/studio-prefs`). Client: `useStudioPrefsSync` (server copy wins; none yet = the browser's copy is pushed up; debounced diff patches). Until the table exists the route answers `stored:false` / `saved:false` and the studio keeps using localStorage, so nothing breaks. Listed in the GDPR export / erase tables (`lib/cyrus/admin/ops.ts`, `data-jobs.server.ts`).
- **Starfield (2).** cyrus.my only (the `CyrusHostProvider` context exists only in `CyrusHostShell`): `components/cyrus/cosmos/Starfield.tsx` replaces the aurora backdrop with pure black, <= 240 stars at alpha <= 0.26, a shooting star every 20-50 s. Canvas 2D at 24 fps, stops while the tab is hidden, no loop and no twinkle under `prefers-reduced-motion`. While it shows, the studio is forced dark (a light studio on black is unreadable). Default on (it is a requested feature of the cyrus.my version only; Nxeon-hosted look is unchanged).
- **Cyrus skin (6).** `app/dashboard/cyrus/ux.css` section 3: `.cyrus-root[data-cy-skin="cyrus"]` re-points the studio's own tokens to the landing's language (black/white hairlines, blue to violet only on primary actions, Space Grotesk display, no blur, no aurora, short ease-out motion) so every component follows; `.cyrus-host[data-cy-skin]` does the cyrus.my bar; the shell's "Back to Nxeon" strip is restyled through `:root:has(.cyrus-root[data-cy-skin="cyrus"])`. OFF until reviewed: `CYRUS_STUDIO_SKIN=1` turns it on for everyone; `?skin=cyrus` / `?skin=nxeon` previews it per browser (`SkinSwitch`). No behaviour or markup changes. Ratchets in `test/cyrus-studio-ux.test.ts` keep every skin rule scoped.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-studio-ux.test.ts`. Screenshots: `scripts/cyrus/studio-ux-shots.mjs` (both hosts x 1440x900 / 1280x720 / 390, with a cut-off diagnosis per page).
EOF
tail -2 docs/cyrus/06-portals.md | cut -c1-80
